title: Normalized proper-open interchange respects successive proper maps
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with the pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaves and finite-subextension convention [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring; sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$ and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Write $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$ for the ordinary unbounded categories and use the module operations of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories; sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback; sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. Let $p:P\to Y$ and $h:P'\to P$ be proper, let $i:Y\hookrightarrow B$ be a quasi-compact open immersion, and let
$$P\xrightarrow{u}W\xrightarrow{r}B,\qquad P'\xrightarrow{v}W'\xrightarrow{s}W$$
be dense compactifications of $ip$ and $uh$, respectively, meaning $u,v$ are quasi-compact scheme-theoretically dense open immersions, $r,s$ proper, $ru=ip$ and $sv=uh$ [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]. For every $A\in D_{P'}$, let
$$I_{Rh_*A}:i_!Rp_*Rh_*A\to Rr_*u_!Rh_*A,\quad J_A:u_!Rh_*A\to Rs_*v_!A,$$
$$I'_A:i_!R(ph)_*A\to R(rs)_*v_!A$$
be the normalized maps of [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange](2), for $(p,i,u,r)$, $(h,u,v,s)$ and $(ph,i,v,rs)$, respectively. Here normalized means that after open restriction and the canonical restriction identifications, composition with the open-extension unit is the identity of the proper direct image. Then the following equality holds for every unbounded $A$, naturally in $A$:
$$\kappa_{r,s,v_!A}\circ I'_A\circ i_!(\kappa_{p,h,A}^{-1})=Rr_*(J_A)\circ I_{Rh_*A}:i_!Rp_*Rh_*A\to Rr_*Rs_*v_!A,$$
where $\kappa$ denotes the canonical derived direct-image comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. No finite-Tor, constructibility or localizing-closure hypothesis on $A$ is required for this equality of maps.

proof.text: Apply [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange](1) first to $(p,i,u,r)$ and then to $(h,u,v,s)$. Thus $r^{-1}(Y)=P$, $s^{-1}(P)=P'$, and $(rs)^{-1}(Y)=P'$ as open subschemes, with restricted maps $p,h,ph$. In particular the two squares and their outer rectangle are Cartesian. The three normalized maps in the statement therefore have the existence and uniqueness in clause (2), for every unbounded input. The outer compactification is one of the three dense compactifications stipulated in the statement. Write $\eta_j:\mathrm{id}\to j^*j_!$ for an open-extension unit.

source.place: Canonicity and associativity, first two sentences; the Cartesian identifications are clause (1) of det-sf-comp-composition-interchange.

proof.text: Use the module adjunction $a^*\dashv a_*$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. By the untwisted last assertion of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], $a^*$ is exact for every map here. By [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf](1), every open restriction $j^*$ is also right adjoint to the exact functor $j_!$, and $\eta_j$ is invertible. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applies both to $a_*$ and to $j^*$: each preserves K-injective complexes. All these statements apply to the pulled-back ring sheaves, including the finite-subextension condensed ring for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. No assertion that open extension preserves K-injectives is used.

For a module sheaf $M$ on $W$, apply [lem-sfb-proetale-open-restriction-counit] to $r$ and $i$, with $R=\Lambda_B$. Identify its inverse-image rings with $\Lambda_W,\Lambda_Y,\Lambda_P$ by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. This gives $i^*r_*M\cong p_*u^*M$; at $Q\to Y$ it is the fibre-product identification $M(W\times_B Q)=M(P\times_Y Q)$ with its transported module action. The same cited result for $(s,u)$ and $(rs,i)$ gives $u^*s_*\cong h_*v^*$ and $i^*(rs)_*\cong(ph)_*v^*$. Its hypothesis is an arbitrary sheaf of commutative rings, so this use requires no constant or finite coefficient ring.

proof.text: Apply the three sheaf isomorphisms of step 3 termwise to K-injective representatives. By step 2 both the restricted complexes and the direct images needed to compute their derived functors remain K-injective. Exact restriction and exact open extension act termwise on every complex by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]; the right derived images are computed on these representatives by [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. We therefore obtain natural isomorphisms $\rho_r:i^*Rr_*\to Rp_*u^*$, $\rho_s:u^*Rs_*\to Rh_*v^*$, and $\rho_{rs}:i^*R(rs)_*\to R(ph)_*v^*$, with exactly the section normalizations of step 3. In particular these are the canonical restriction identifications used to normalize $I,J,I'$ in the statement.

proof.text:
For $B_0\in D_{W'}$ put $\chi_{B_0}=Rp_*(\rho_{s,B_0})\circ\rho_{r,Rs_*B_0}$. The specified comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] gives
$$\chi_{B_0}\circ i^*(\kappa_{r,s,B_0})=\kappa_{p,h,v^*B_0}\circ\rho_{rs,B_0}.$$
Indeed, choose a K-injective representative $H$ of $B_0$. Step 2 makes $s_*H$, $v^*H$, and $h_*v^*H$ K-injective, so the extra resolutions in the cited normalization can be chosen to be identities. At $Q\to Y$, both sides of the display are the section identification on the same complex $H(W'\times_B Q)=H(P'\times_Y Q)$: the successive fibre-product identifications of step 3 equal the direct one. The module actions are the same restricted actions. Thus the degreewise maps coincide before localization. This proves the displayed identity with these particular $\kappa$'s, rather than unspecified direct-image isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, with its K-injective normalization; the section identities of step 3.

proof.text:
Set $X=Rh_*A$, $t_A=\eta_{v,A}^{-1}$, $F_A=Rr_*(J_A)\circ I_X$, and
$$L_A=Rp_*Rh_*(t_A)\circ\chi_{v_!A}:i^*Rr_*Rs_*v_!A\longrightarrow Rp_*Rh_*A.$$
The two given normalizations say
$$Rp_*(\eta_{u,X}^{-1})\rho_{r,u_!X}\,i^*I_X\,\eta_{i,Rp_*X}=1,\qquad Rh_*(t_A)\rho_{s,v_!A}\,u^*J_A\,\eta_{u,X}=1.$$
Naturality of $\rho_r$ at $J_A$ now gives, by substitution,
$$L_A\,i^*F_A\,\eta_{i,Rp_*X}=Rp_*\bigl(Rh_*(t_A)\rho_{s,v_!A}\,u^*J_A\bigr)\rho_{r,u_!X}\,i^*I_X\,\eta_{i,Rp_*X}=1.$$
Here the second normalization replaces the parenthesis by $\eta_{u,X}^{-1}$, and the first normalization gives the final identity. All inverses used are open units, which are invertible by step 2; invertibility of $I$ or $J$ is unnecessary.

source.place: Canonicity and associativity: the two composites have the same open normalization; explicit substitution into clause (2) of det-sf-comp-composition-interchange.

proof.text:
Put $\lambda_A=R(ph)_*(t_A)\rho_{rs,v_!A}$. Step 5 and naturality of $\kappa_{p,h}$ at $t_A$ give
$$L_A\,i^*\kappa_{r,s,v_!A}=\kappa_{p,h,A}\lambda_A.$$
Consider $G_A=\kappa_{r,s,v_!A}^{-1}F_A\,i_!(\kappa_{p,h,A}):i_!R(ph)_*A\to R(rs)_*v_!A$. Using this display, naturality of $\eta_i$, and step 6, its normalization is
$$\lambda_A\,i^*G_A\,\eta_{i,R(ph)_*A}=\kappa_{p,h,A}^{-1}\bigl(L_A\,i^*F_A\,\eta_{i,Rp_*Rh_*A}\bigr)\kappa_{p,h,A}=1.$$
The uniqueness assertion of [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange](2), applied to $(ph,i,v,rs)$, yields $G_A=I'_A$. Multiplying by $\kappa_{r,s,v_!A}$ and $i_!(\kappa_{p,h,A}^{-1})$ proves exactly the required equality. All factors and the restriction identifications are natural; hence it holds naturally in $A$. The proof used only K-injectives, exact pullback and open extension, so applies to every unbounded $A$.
